mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes during a tightening cycle.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes when GDPC1 is falling.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of triggered months with UNRATE > 5.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which raises input costs and dampens earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes with INDPRO below its 12-month MA for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3% signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which erodes real purchasing power and increases financing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered months when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive correlation between housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) over the past six months signals coordinated demand recovery, which boosts earnings expectations and equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes with strong HOUST-INDPRO correlation.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) growth above 0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS MoM growth > 0.5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of triggered episodes with PAYEMS MoM growth > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing firms and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes when RSAFS is below its 12-month MA for four months.
